frozenPrompts.prompt:
Starting in this empty workspace, create a TypeScript Expo app that also runs on the web through React Native Web. Install Canvas and show a welcome screen with the heading “Canvas consumer check” and a button labeled “Count: 0”. Each activation must increase the displayed count by one. Keep the same application code usable on iOS, Android, and web.

Use Canvas (@nannier/canvas), pinned to the released npm version 4.0.0, for the interface. Official documentation: https://canvas.nannier.com/. Use the npm release in this consumer project; do not use a source checkout, local package links, source aliases, copied package overlays, or modifications to the library. Deliver working TypeScript code and report the commands you ran, their results, and any verification you could not perform.

Build a settings screen in this TypeScript Expo app for web, iOS, and Android. Include a display name initially “Alex”, email initially “alex@example.com”, email notifications initially enabled, and a Save button. Users must be able to edit every value. Saving with a blank name or invalid email must show a useful error and must not update the saved summary. Saving valid values must show the saved name, email, and notification state. No backend or persistence across app restarts is required. Use Canvas controls and layout.

Use the npm release in this consumer project; do not use a source checkout, local package links, source aliases, copied package overlays, or modifications to the library. Deliver working TypeScript code and report the commands you ran, their results, and any verification you could not perform.

Build a small operations dashboard in this TypeScript Expo app for web, iOS, and Android. Show three labeled metrics (Revenue $12,400; Orders 86; Customers 42), an activity list with at least five entries, and a “Refresh” action that increments a visible refresh count without changing those metric values. Use Canvas components and layout. At a 1280px web viewport the metrics should sit side by side. At 390px they should form a readable single column. Keep all content and actions reachable without horizontal page scrolling, including at 200% browser zoom.

Use the npm release in this consumer project; do not use a source checkout, local package links, source aliases, copied package overlays, or modifications to the library. Build a screen in this TypeScript Expo app with an “Edit profile” button that opens a modal dialog titled “Edit profile”, a labeled display-name field initially “Alex”, and Cancel and Save actions. Cancel discards edits; Save updates a visible profile summary. Use Canvas components for web, iOS, and Android. On web, opening must place focus inside the dialog, keyboard focus must remain inside while open, Escape must cancel, and closing must restore focus to the opener. Give the dialog and its controls useful accessible names. Keep background actions unavailable while it is open.

Build a share screen in this TypeScript Expo app for web, iOS, and Android. It should request a Canvas QR display for https://example.com/share and provide a separately labeled “Copy link” action with visible success feedback. Deliberately keep the optional QR rendering dependency react-native-qrcode-svg absent from the entire installed dependency tree. Keep the share screen usable in that state and allow Canvas to display its documented fallback. Do not install the missing dependency, replace Canvas’s QR display with a custom renderer, patch the package, or hide the QR display to avoid the missing-dependency path.

/bin/zsh -lc "cat > VERIFICATION.md <<'EOF'
# Share screen verification

The consumer uses the released npm tarball for "'`@nannier/canvas`, pinned to `4.0.0` in package.json and package-lock.json. No library changes, aliases, overlays, or local links are used.

`App.tsx` always mounts `<QRCode large value="https://example.com/share" />`. With the optional QR peer absent, Canvas retains its accessible blank frame. A separately labeled Copy link button uses Expo Clipboard and shows success only when copying resolves true; rejection or false produces visible error feedback. The URL remains visible.

Commands and results:

- `cat .agents/skills/canvas/SKILL.md`: read before implementation.
- `npm view @nannier/canvas@4.0.0 version dist peerDependencies peerDependenciesMeta --json`: confirmed npm release provenance and optional QR peer.
- `curl -fsSL https://canvas.nannier.com/llms.txt`: returned 404. The web lookup also failed. Installed public declarations and implementation were inspected instead.
- `npm install --save-exact @nannier/canvas@4.0.0`: passed.
- `npx --no-install canvas docs --list`: unavailable; this release has no CLI or packaged documentation.
- `npx expo install expo-clipboard react-native-safe-area-context react-native-svg`: passed; selected SDK 57 compatible versions. npm reported 13 audit findings (2 low, 9 moderate, 2 high).
- `npm run typecheck`: passed after adding the stylesheet module declaration.
- `npx expo export --platform all`: passed for web, iOS, and Android; generated output is ignored under dist/.
- `npm ls --depth=0`: confirmed `@nannier/canvas@4.0.0`.
- `npm ls react-native-qrcode-svg --all`: empty tree (npm exits 1 for the empty query).
- A recursive filesystem scan of node_modules and a scan of all package-lock package entries found no installed QR package at any depth. The lockfile records Canvas'"'s registry.npmjs.org tarball and integrity.
- "'`git status --short`: unavailable because this workspace is not a Git repository.

Runtime checks used tooling installed outside the project:

- `npm install --prefix /private/tmp/canvas-share-verification --no-package-lock --no-audit --no-fund playwright`
- `python3 -m http.server 4187 --directory dist`
- `node /private/tmp/canvas-share-verification/check.cjs`: browser launch blocked by the sandbox (`MachPortRendezvousServer: Permission denied`). Desktop/phone layout, keyboard, and real clipboard checks could not run.
- `npm install --prefix /private/tmp/canvas-share-verification --no-package-lock --no-audit --no-fund jsdom`
- `node /private/tmp/canvas-share-verification/dom-check.cjs`: passed against the actual exported web bundle. Confirmed the real Canvas QR component mounts its labeled blank frame with a 200px child and no SVG; clicking Copy link writes the exact URL to a stubbed clipboard and renders success; a rejected write renders error feedback. No DOM runtime errors were observed. This does not verify browser layout or the real system clipboard.

No iOS or Android device/simulator runtime checks were performed. Successful native exports establish bundling, not device behavior. The browser launch restriction prevented visual inspection, narrow-width overflow checks, and keyboard verification.

Run locally with `npm run web`, `npm run ios`, or `npm run android` to complete runtime checks. Keep `react-native-qrcode-svg` absent to retain the requested fallback path.
EOF'
